94-038.r: Jagar → ancestor-spirit worship ritual in the hills of Uttarakhand (Kumaon, Garhwal); gods and local deities are invoked for remedies.

94-039.r: Rath Yatra festival → Jagannath Puri, Odisha.

94-040.r: Maluti village (Dumka district, Jharkhand) → known as the 'village of temples'.

94-041.r: Wrong pair: Sadhvi Sadhana → Jain Sant, not homemaker doctor. Correct: Madhumita Raut → Odissi dancer; Indira Chakravarty → nutrition scientist; Meera Bhatia → jurist.

94-042.r: Bhajan Sopori → Santoor (Sufiana Gharana, Kashmir); Birju Maharaj → Kathak (Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana); Priyadarshini Govind → Bharatnatyam; T.V. Gopala Krishnan → Mridangam.

94-043.r: Ustad Alla Rakha (Qureshi) → Tabla player; father of Ustad Zakir Hussain.

94-044.r: Wrong pair: Panna Lal Ghosh → flute (Bansuri), not Tabla. Correct: Debu Chaudhuri → Sitar; Amjad Ali Khan → Sarod; Yehudi Menuhin → Violin.

94-045.r: Correct pair: Pampa → Kannada; his 'Vikramarjuna Vijaya' is the Kannada version of the Mahabharata.

94-046.r: First writer to use Urdu for poetry → Amir Khusrau; also known as originator of Qawwali.

94-047.r: 'Radha Govind Sangeet Sar' (classical music work) → Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.

94-048.r: Dhrupad: primarily devotional; Alap uses Sanskrit mantra syllables. Wrong: 'Mughal-period Rajput origin' — it began earlier, from Vedic chanting, with Gwalior's Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516).

94-049.r: Umakant and Ramakant Gundecha (Gundecha Brothers) → Dagarvani Dhrupad vocalists, born in Ujjain.

94-050.r: 'Raga Kalpadrum' → Krishnanand Vyas. Sangeetraj → Maharana Kumbha; Sringarhar → Rana Hammir; Rag Ratnakar → Radhakrishna.

94-051.r: Raga Todi → early morning; Bhimpalasi → afternoon; Bhopali → evening; Darbari → night.

94-052.r: Chakiarkoothu: performed only by the Chakiar community; Mizhavu drum accompanies; staged in temple theatre Koothambalam. Statement on higher castes not watching is wrong.

94-053.r: Manipuri Sankirtana → singing, drumming and dancing narrating Lord Krishna's life (on UNESCO intangible heritage list). Wrong: cymbals are not the only instruments.

94-054.r: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi → Hindustani classical (Khayal) singer of the Kirana Gharana; Bharat Ratna 2009.

94-056.r: Kalamandalam Kshemavathy → Mohiniattam; Kottakkal Sivaraman → Kathakali; Lakshmi Viswanathan → Bharatanatyam; N. Madhabi Devi → Manipuri.

94-057.r: Bharatanatyam → Tamil Nadu; Kathak → Uttar Pradesh; Kuchipudi → Andhra Pradesh; Mohiniattam → Kerala.

94-058.r: Bharatanatyam → Tamil Nadu; Kuchipudi → Andhra Pradesh; Sattriya → Assam; Kathak → Uttar Pradesh.

94-059.r: Odissi → one of the eight classical dances of India; from Odisha (Orissa).

94-060.r: Mohiniattam → Kerala; performed by women; 'Mohini' = maiden who steals the onlooker's heart; one of the eight classical dances.

94-061.r: Sattriya (Assam) → music, dance and drama; centuries-old Vaishnavite tradition begun by Sankaradeva; classical status 2000. Wrong: not based on Tulsidas-Kabir-Mirabai songs.

94-062.r: Solo dance → Mohiniattam (Kerala), performed as solo recitals by women; main theme 'sringara' (love).

94-063.r: Correct: Garba → Gujarat; Yakshagana (folk theatre) → Karnataka. Wrong: Mohiniattam → Kerala, not Odisha.

94-064.r: Latest Indian entry on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list (of options) → Garba of Gujarat (Dec 2023), devotional Navaratri dance.

94-065.r: Kuchipudi dancers sometimes speak dialogue (not in Bharatanatyam). Dancing on brass-plate edges (Tarangam) is Kuchipudi's feature, not Bharatanatyam's.
94-065.t: Brass-plate dance (Tarangam) belongs to Kuchipudi, not Bharatanatyam.

94-066.r: Kathak → classical dance whose present form shows Mughal influence.

94-067.r: Hiren Bhattacharya → Puppetry; Malini Rajurkar → Hindustani vocal music; Pratibha Prahlad → Bharatnatyam; Vempati Chinna Satyam → Kuchipudi.

94-068.r: Manipuri → dance from eastern (North-Eastern) India, Manipur; Kathakali, Kuchipudi and Bharatnatyam are South Indian.

94-069.r: Indrani Rahman (1930-1999) → classical dancer of Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali and Odissi; the commission's key gave Odissi.
94-069.c: No answer printed: she performed several styles; the official key chose (c) Odissi.

94-070.r: Girija Devi, famous Thumri singer → Banaras Gharana.

94-071.r: Book answer: Sarangi is not of Indo-Islamic origin; Sitar and Tabla are credited to Amir Khusrau.
94-071.c: Muddled: explanation says Turks brought Rabab and Sarangi, yet answers Sarangi; MPPSC key marked (d) Shehnai.

94-072.r: Gangubai Hangal (1913-2009) → Hindustani classical Khayal singer of the Kirana Gharana, known for her deep, powerful voice.

94-073.r: Tera Tali → folk dance of Rajasthan, performed sitting on the ground by women of the Kamar tribe.

94-074.r: Wrong pair: Yakshagana → Karnataka (coastal Udupi, Dakshina Kannada), not Rajasthan. Correct: Kaikottikali → Kerala women; Koli → Maharashtra; Himachali → Kullu Valley.

94-075.r: Andhra Pradesh → Burra; Assam → Bihu; Himachal Pradesh → Nati; Rajasthan → Ghoomar.

94-076.r: Assam → Ojapali; Himachal Pradesh → Luddi; West Bengal → Jatra; Bihar → Jata-Jatin.

94-077.r: Karagam → religious folk dance of Tamil Nadu.

94-078.r: Shahnai → Bismillah Khan; Sarod → Amjad Ali Khan; Painter → Maqbool Fida Husain; Tabla → Alla Rakha; Sitar → Ravi Shankar.

94-079.r: Wrong pair: Amjad Ali Khan → Sarod ('Sarod Samrat'), not Pakhawaj. Correct: Vilayat Khan → Sitar; Alla Rakha → Tabla; Hari Prasad Chaurasia → Flute.

94-080.r: Birju Maharaj → Kathak; Hari Prasad Chaurasia → Flute; Ali Akbar → Sarod; Zakir Hussain → Tabla.

94-081.r: V.G. Jog → Violin. Ravishankar → Sitar; Zakir Hussain → Tabla; Shivkumar Sharma → Santoor.

94-082.r: Akum and Todi → wind instruments, like Bansuri, Mohuri (Madhukari), Shankh.

94-083.r: 'Toti' → traditional parrot-shaped earring of Rajasthani women (silver or gold, with red or green stone).

94-084.r: Shiv Kumar Sharma → Santoor; Hari Prasad Chaurasia → Flute; Asad Ali Khan → Rudra Veena; Pramod Gaekwad → Sundari.
